hunt.name: Unsigned Payloads and DLL Side-Loading Tagged by Defender
hunt.description:
Defender notes things about files that it does not alert on. When an unsigned PE is created it sets NewPECreatedNoCert on the path; when one runs, ExecutedPENoCert; when behaviour monitoring sees a likely side-load, BM_IsPotentialSideLoad; when a new archive appears, NewlyCreatedZip. It also queues executables it saw dropped and then executed. These tags sit in mpenginedb.db for about two weeks.

This hunt reads the tags on every Windows host through the defender_mpengine osquery extension, keeps those in user-writable folders, and adds the file's current hash and signature. Stacking hashes across the fleet removes installers and updaters, and file-write telemetry shows which browser, archive tool or messaging client wrote each one. It first counts every tag the fleet produces, because the tag names are undocumented and others may matter.

Suspect files are then checked for side-loading (an unsigned DLL loaded from the same folder as the signed program loading it) and for what they started, before an agent and an analyst decide.

meta.name: Unsigned Payloads and DLL Side-Loading Tagged by Defender
meta.hypothesis: A loader delivered through a browser download, archive or messaging app wrote an unsigned executable, or a DLL beside a signed program, into a user-writable folder and ran it, and Defender tagged the file without raising a detection.
meta.rationale: Run across all Windows workstations first; servers rarely have user-space executables. Paste the hosts staging-triage names into scope_hosts before the module and process steps.
meta.analysis: Tags fire on every installer that unpacks to AppData. Separating a payload from an updater takes the fleet-wide hash count, the writing process, the signature and what the file started.

hunt.justification: Commodity loaders, ClickFix payloads and side-loaded implants all pass through this step, and Defender has already flagged the files on hosts with no EDR.

references.name: Protokol-7 — Defender's hidden flight recorder: mpenginedb.db

related.reason: Reads what Defender scored the payload's process for once it ran.

scenario.summary: A lure leads a user to download or extract a payload into a user-writable folder. The payload is an unsigned executable, or a signed program with a malicious DLL beside it, and it runs. Defender tags the files but does not detect them.

stages.name: Payload written to user space
observables: Browser, archive tool or messaging app writing a PE

stages.name: DLL side-loaded by a signed program
observables: ffmpeg.dll or pcaui.dll in unusual folders

coverage.reason: The mail, chat or web lure that delivered the file is in mail and proxy telemetry; this hunt starts at the file on disk.

blind_spots.requires: the defender_mpengine osquery extension loaded by osqueryd (running as SYSTEM) on every Windows host, with Microsoft Defender Antivirus as the active engine and defender_mpengine_status.error empty
blind_spots.question: Did Defender record anything on hosts where the extension is missing, cannot decrypt the database, or Defender is passive behind another antivirus?
blind_spots.risk: Those hosts return no rows, which looks the same as a clean host. An attacker who has removed or stopped Defender also leaves an empty or stale database.
blind_spots.remediation: Deploy the extension through extensions.load on all Windows hosts and alert on defender_mpengine_status rows with a non-empty error.

blind_spots.requires: path tags younger than their expire_time (about two weeks)
blind_spots.question: Was an unsigned payload run before the tags expired?
blind_spots.risk: Older drops leave no tag; schedule the pack query to keep them.

blind_spots.question: Exactly when does Defender set each tag?
blind_spots.risk: Meanings are inferred from the names and Protokol-7's observations.

blind_spots.requires: the file still on disk, or MFT and USN journal data
blind_spots.question: What was a tagged file that has since been deleted?
blind_spots.risk: hash and authenticode return nothing for a missing file. Defender's hash cache keeps the hash but only an MFT reference, not the path.

blind_spots.requires: code-signing reputation beyond signed or unsigned
blind_spots.question: Was the payload signed with a stolen or abused certificate?
blind_spots.risk: NoCert tags never fire for signed payloads; only the side-load tag and rarity still apply.

blind_spots.requires: image-load events (Sysmon event 7 or EDR) in hb_module_activity
blind_spots.question: Did the signed program actually load the tagged DLL?
blind_spots.risk: Image loads are often not collected for volume; side-loading then rests on Defender's tag alone.

lookback_days.description: Days of history to examine. Defender keeps roughly two weeks in mpenginedb.db.

scope_hosts.description: Hosts to focus the follow-up queries on, as osquery reports their hostname; empty runs them across the estate.

pe_path_tags.description: Defender path tags that mark unsigned PEs created or run, likely side-loading and new archives. Add tags path-tag-inventory reveals.

config.description: Count every path tag the engine set in the window, per host. Microsoft does not document these tags; this shows which ones this fleet produces and how common each is, so a tag that is rare here, or one not yet in pe_path_tags, stands out.
config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, context, COUNT(*) AS tagged_paths, MIN(insert_time) AS first_tagged, MAX(insert_time) AS last_tagged FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context WHERE record_kind = 'path_tag' AND file_path != 'MpTamperProtectionState' AND insert_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400) GROUP BY context
config.expected_signal: NewPECreatedNoCert and NewlyCreatedZip on most hosts; ExecutedPENoCert and BM_IsPotentialSideLoad on fewer. A tag present on one or two hosts only is worth reading in full.

primitive_config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, context, COUNT(*) AS tagged_paths, MIN(insert_time) AS first_tagged, MAX(insert_time) AS last_tagged FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context WHERE record_kind = 'path_tag' AND file_path != 'MpTamperProtectionState' AND insert_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400) GROUP BY context
primitive_config.label: Every path tag Defender wrote
primitive_config.expected: NewPECreatedNoCert and NewlyCreatedZip on most hosts; ExecutedPENoCert and BM_IsPotentialSideLoad on fewer. A tag present on one or two hosts only is worth reading in full.

config.description: For each tagged file in a user-writable folder, collect every tag it carries, its current SHA-256 and its signature status. A file that is both NewPECreatedNoCert and ExecutedPENoCert was dropped unsigned and then run; a DLL tagged BM_IsPotentialSideLoad is sitting where a signed program will load it.
config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, t.file_path, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT t.context) AS tags, MIN(t.insert_time) AS first_tagged, MAX(t.insert_time) AS last_tagged, MAX(h.sha256) AS sha256, MAX(a.result) AS signature_result, MAX(a.subject_name) AS signer FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context t LEFT JOIN hash h ON h.path = t.file_path LEFT JOIN authenticode a ON a.path = t.file_path WHERE t.record_kind = 'path_tag' AND t.insert_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400) AND instr(',' || LOWER('{{pe_path_tags}}') || ',', ',' || LOWER(t.context) || ',') > 0 AND (LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%') GROUP BY t.file_path
config.expected_signal: Installers and updaters unpacking under AppData appear on many hosts with the same SHA-256. An unsigned PE created and executed on one or two hosts, or a side-load candidate beside a signed binary, is the lead. sha256 is empty when the file is gone.

primitive_config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, t.file_path, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT t.context) AS tags, MIN(t.insert_time) AS first_tagged, MAX(t.insert_time) AS last_tagged, MAX(h.sha256) AS sha256, MAX(a.result) AS signature_result, MAX(a.subject_name) AS signer FROM defender_mpengine_persist_context t LEFT JOIN hash h ON h.path = t.file_path LEFT JOIN authenticode a ON a.path = t.file_path WHERE t.record_kind = 'path_tag' AND t.insert_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400) AND instr(',' || LOWER('{{pe_path_tags}}') || ',', ',' || LOWER(t.context) || ',') > 0 AND (LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(t.file_path) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%') GROUP BY t.file_path
primitive_config.label: Tagged files in user-writable folders
primitive_config.expected: Installers and updaters unpacking under AppData appear on many hosts with the same SHA-256. An unsigned PE created and executed on one or two hosts, or a side-load candidate beside a signed binary, is the lead. sha256 is empty when the file is gone.

nodes.label: Executables Defender saw dropped and run

config.description: Read the RQ_RecentExecDropped queues, where the engine lists executables it saw written and then executed.
config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, entry_key AS dropped_path, queue, insert_time, expire_time FROM defender_mpengine_rolling_queues WHERE queue_type = 'dropped_executable' AND insert_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400)
config.expected_signal: Paths such as AppData\Local\Temp\7zS...\setup.exe. A path that is also in tagged-user-space-files confirms drop-and-run.

primitive_config.content: SELECT (SELECT hostname FROM system_info) AS device_hostname, entry_key AS dropped_path, queue, insert_time, expire_time FROM defender_mpengine_rolling_queues WHERE queue_type = 'dropped_executable' AND insert_time >= (CAST(strftime('%s', 'now') AS INTEGER) - {{lookback_days}} * 86400)
primitive_config.label: Executables Defender saw dropped and run
primitive_config.expected: Paths such as AppData\Local\Temp\7zS...\setup.exe. A path that is also in tagged-user-space-files confirms drop-and-run.

nodes.label: Rare executables written to user space

config.description: Stack every executable or DLL written to a user-writable folder by SHA-256 across the fleet, with the processes that wrote it. A browser, archive tool or messaging client writing a binary seen on fewer than three hosts is how most loaders arrive.
config.content: SELECT file_hash_sha256, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_list, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT process_name) AS writers, MIN(file_path) AS example_path, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_file_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.exe' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.dll' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.scr' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.cpl') AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%') AND file_hash_sha256 IS NOT NULL AND file_hash_sha256 != '' GROUP BY file_hash_sha256 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) < 3
config.expected_signal: Rare hashes with the writing process. Browser, 7-Zip, WinRAR, Explorer (zip extraction), Teams, Slack, Telegram or Discord as writer marks delivery.

primitive_config.content: SELECT file_hash_sha256, COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS hosts, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT device_hostname) AS host_list, GROUP_CONCAT(DISTINCT process_name) AS writers, MIN(file_path) AS example_path, MIN(time) AS first_seen FROM hb_file_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.exe' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.dll' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.scr' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%.cpl') AND (LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(file_path) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%') AND file_hash_sha256 IS NOT NULL AND file_hash_sha256 != '' GROUP BY file_hash_sha256 HAVING COUNT(DISTINCT device_hostname) < 3
primitive_config.label: Rare executables written to user space
primitive_config.expected: Rare hashes with the writing process. Browser, 7-Zip, WinRAR, Explorer (zip extraction), Teams, Slack, Telegram or Discord as writer marks delivery.

nodes.label: Which tagged files were delivered payloads

config.description: Combine Defender's tags with how each file arrived.
config.objective: For each file from tagged-user-space-files, decide whether it looks like a delivered payload: unsigned and both created and executed, a side-load candidate DLL beside a signed executable, preceded by a NewlyCreatedZip in the same profile, listed in dropped-then-executed, and rare across the fleet by SHA-256 or written by a browser, archive tool or messaging client. Discount files whose SHA-256 appears on many hosts.
config.success_criteria: A list of suspect files with host, path, tags, SHA-256 and writer, citing rows; the hosts to paste into scope_hosts.

nodes.label: Unsigned DLLs loaded from the loader's own folder

config.description: Confirm side-loading: a process loading a DLL that is not validly signed from the same user-writable folder as its own image.
config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, process_name, module_path, module_signed, module_signature_status, module_signature_subject, module_hash_sha256 FROM hb_module_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%.dll' AND (LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%') AND LOWER(COALESCE(CAST(module_signed AS TEXT), '')) NOT IN ('1', 'true') AND LOWER(rtrim(module_path, replace(module_path, '\', ''))) = LOWER(rtrim(process_name, replace(process_name, '\', '')))
config.expected_signal: A signed executable in AppData or ProgramData loading an unsigned DLL from its own folder. Protokol-7's examples were ffmpeg.dll and pcaui.dll in uncommon places.

primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, process_name, module_path, module_signed, module_signature_status, module_signature_subject, module_hash_sha256 FROM hb_module_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%.dll' AND (LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(module_path) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%') AND LOWER(COALESCE(CAST(module_signed AS TEXT), '')) NOT IN ('1', 'true') AND LOWER(rtrim(module_path, replace(module_path, '\', ''))) = LOWER(rtrim(process_name, replace(process_name, '\', '')))
primitive_config.label: Unsigned DLLs loaded from the loader's own folder
primitive_config.expected: A signed executable in AppData or ProgramData loading an unsigned DLL from its own folder. Protokol-7's examples were ffmpeg.dll and pcaui.dll in uncommon places.

config.description: Show the user-space images that ran on the suspect hosts, their parents and children, to see what each payload started.
config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, user_name, parent_process_name, process_name, process_cmd_line, process_hash_sha256 FROM hb_process_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND ((LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%') OR (LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%'))
config.expected_signal: The suspect image with its parent (browser, Explorer, archive tool) and the processes it started. Script hosts or LOLBins as children are the next stage.

primitive_config.content: SELECT device_hostname, time, user_name, parent_process_name, process_name, process_cmd_line, process_hash_sha256 FROM hb_process_activity WHERE time >= datetime('now', '-{{lookback_days}} days') AND ('{{scope_hosts}}' = '' OR instr(',' || '{{scope_hosts}}' || ',', ',' || device_hostname || ',') > 0) AND ((LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(process_name) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%') OR (LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\users\%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\programdata\%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\windows\temp\%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\perflogs\%' OR LOWER(parent_process_name) LIKE '%\$recycle.bin\%'))
primitive_config.label: Execution from user-writable folders
primitive_config.expected: The suspect image with its parent (browser, Explorer, archive tool) and the processes it started. Script hosts or LOLBins as children are the next stage.

config.description: Decide which suspect files are malicious.
config.objective: For each file from staging-triage, decide malicious, suspicious or benign from its signature, rarity, writer, side-load evidence and what it started. A vendor updater on many hosts is benign; an unsigned, rare DLL loaded by a signed binary in AppData that then starts PowerShell is malicious.
config.success_criteria: A verdict per file and host citing rows from each step.

config.description: Act on malicious payloads; send unclear ones to a person.
config.condition: staging-verdict finds at least one malicious payload
config.question: staging-verdict finds at least one malicious payload

config.description: Stop the payload and preserve it.
config.instructions: Collect the suspect file and the host's Scans folder. Isolate the host, run a Defender custom scan of the file's folder, and quarantine the file if the scan does not.
Check each suspect file's Zone.Identifier stream for its download URL and the messages or mails that delivered it. Search the SHA-256 across the estate, and submit unknown files for analysis.

config.description: Record results and keep the signal.
config.instructions: Record findings. Keep the benign SHA-256 values as an allow list, and schedule tagged-user-space-files as a pack query so new rare unsigned payloads surface daily.
